stumbles.quote: Oskar asked the question on 2026-11-09: "does that mean we could trim these to 256 length vectors without penalty by reversing the widening?"
stumbles.why: Oskar is unexplained, and the quote refers to a prior conversation ('that', 'the widening') that the reader never saw.

stumbles.quote: the quantized 256-dimensional codes are smaller than the live 768-dimensional index and have higher recall
stumbles.why: This conflicts with the table and later text. At 2 bits the 256-d codes are worse. The 3-bit codes are 104 bytes against 200 bytes, so they are smaller, but 'live index' is not defined at this point.

stumbles.quote: The live index stores 2 bits × 768 dimensions in 200 bytes
stumbles.why: 2 bits × 768 dimensions is 192 bytes, so 200 bytes implies some overhead the text never explains. The 'live index' is also never introduced.
The byte count is missing for the 2-bit row, so the size comparison at equal bit width cannot be checked.
The table's 'Recall@10' is not defined. It is unclear whether it is measured against float search, and it is a different metric from the 'hit@10' used earlier.

stumbles.quote: Here are the results for remex codes on the 256 folded dimensions
stumbles.why: 'remex' is never explained. It is apparently a quantizer, and the text later says it has a rotation.

stumbles.quote: Remex's rotation also folds into the same matrix, so the model can emit rotated coordinates directly. With an int8 head, this reaches 0.931 recall@10 at 4 bits.
stumbles.why: 'int8 head' is unexplained. It is unclear what this result is compared against, and whether it is the same setup as the 0.927 in the table.

stumbles.quote: The List Scout page now runs the folded model.
stumbles.why: 'List Scout page' is an unexplained name, and so is the site it belongs to. 'Classifier answers' and 'fitting' are also undefined.

stumbles.quote: without any loss in float search
stumbles.why: This is only loosely supported. The evidence is equal hit@10 and score agreement within 1.1e-06, and the text never says whether the 256-d model is a different model or only a folded matrix.

point: Folding Ettin-17m's output matrix to 256 dimensions leaves float search unchanged, and 3–4-bit quantized 256-d codes beat the live 2-bit 768-d index on recall at smaller size, though many terms and baselines are left unexplained.
